evidence: server.py:53 `mcp = FastMCP("i14y-mcp")` — constructor receives no `lifespan=` argument.
No `@asynccontextmanager` / `AsyncExitStack` anywhere in src/ (grep returned no matches).
server.py:64-66 `_get()` does `async with build_client() as http:` — a fresh httpx.AsyncClient is created and torn down per tool call.
client.py:63-69 `build_client()` returns a new `httpx.AsyncClient(...)` with docstring 'Caller owns the lifecycle.' — no shared/pooled client.
server.py:api_status also opens its own `async with build_client() as http:` per call.
gaps: This is exactly the check's documented fail-pattern (new httpx.AsyncClient per call): no connection-pool reuse across requests, cleanup tied to each call instead of a server lifespan.
No lifespan function with @asynccontextmanager; FastMCP not given lifespan=; no server.state resource holding.
Single-server setup so AsyncExitStack criterion is N/A, but zero of the applicable pass-criteria are met.

evidence: pyproject.toml:27 `pydantic>=2.7` in dependencies (>=2.0).
models.py:1 docstring 'Pydantic v2 models'; models.py:11 imports `BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field`; uses `model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")` (v2 API, not v1 Config class).
Every tool in server.py has an explicit BaseModel return annotation (e.g. `-> SearchResult`, `-> DatasetListResult`, `-> DistributionsResult`, `-> StatusResult`).

Consistent response envelope: models.py:22 `I14YResponse` base carries `source`, `provenance`, `retrieved_at`; all result models inherit it and add `returned`/`total_matched`/`hits` (envelope equivalents of results/count).
models.py:15 `Provenance = Literal["live_api", "cached"]` — Literal type for enumerable value; RESOURCE_TYPES/Language also Literals in server.py.
Defaults use `Field(default_factory=list)` for mutable list fields (models.py:87,131,132,147, etc.) — no bare mutable defaults.
gaps: Envelope field names differ from the check's illustrative names (`returned`/`hits` rather than `count`/`results`) — cosmetic only; the source+provenance+count+results semantics are all present and applied uniformly.

evidence: No tool declares a `ctx: Context` parameter; `Context` is never imported from `mcp.server.fastmcp` in server.py.
No `ctx.report_progress`, `ctx.info`, `ctx.warning`, `ctx.error`, `ctx.elicit`, or `ctx.sample` calls anywhere in src/.
Positive: no `print()` or direct stdlib `logging` inside tool bodies — so the stdio-transport protocol-crash anti-pattern is avoided.
Tools are single upstream GETs; the only loop is api_status over 3 fixed endpoints (server.py) — no long iteration / gather over many tasks.
gaps: Zero Context adoption: no structured logging or client-visible observability via the MCP protocol.

client.py sets TIMEOUT_S=60 with retry backoff 2s/4s/8s (MAX_ATTEMPTS=4), so a degraded upstream call can plausibly exceed the check's 2s progress threshold with no `ctx.report_progress` feedback to the client.
Read-only server has no writing tools, so the ctx.elicit (HITL) criterion is N/A; the short single-fetch nature of the tools makes the progress gap low-impact but still unaddressed.

evidence: Transport is dual: server.py main() honours `I14Y_MCP_TRANSPORT` and runs `mcp.run(transport="sse")` or `"streamable-http"` — so the HTTP/SSE applies_when is active.
No CORS configuration exists: grep for `CORSMiddleware|cors|allow_origins|expose_headers|middleware` across src/ returns no matches.
Server exposes HTTP/SSE via `mcp.run(...)` on `mcp.settings.host`/`port` directly — no custom Starlette/ASGI app, no CORSMiddleware, no `cors_expose_headers` passed to FastMCP.
No `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: Mcp-Session-Id` is configured anywhere.
gaps: `expose_headers` does not include `Mcp-Session-Id` (not set at all) — browser cross-origin clients cannot read the session id, so stateful SSE sessions break while stdio/server-side curl tests pass.

Mitigating context (not a pass): server is read-only and no-auth, so session-state breakage is less damaging than for an authed stateful server, but none of the applicable pass-criteria are satisfied.

evidence: Attribution is structurally enforced: models.py:22-29 `I14YResponse` (base of every outbound payload) has `source: str = Field(default=ATTRIBUTION)`; docstring notes 'omitting attribution and provenance structurally impossible'.

client.py:14-19 `ATTRIBUTION` names provider + URL: 'Data: I14Y Interoperability Platform, Swiss Federal Statistical Office (BFS) — https://www.i14y.admin.ch. Licence terms are declared per distribution; check the `licence` field before reuse.'

Per-distribution licence is surfaced: models.py:116 and :182 `licence: str | None`; get_dataset_distributions (server.py) returns each distribution with its own licence; README.md:108,195-197 document that licences vary per distribution ('Opendata BY ASK', attribution required).

README documents the data source and licensing: README.md:233 'Data: I14Y Interoperability Platform, Federal Statistical Office (BFS)'; README.md:239 'catalogue data remains subject to the terms declared by each publisher' (MIT applies to code only).
Provenance retained per record (licence lives on each Distribution, not just globally); provenance field present on every envelope.
gaps: README has no formal source/licence table as in the check's template; licensing is described in prose + per-distribution field.

The data is not uniformly CC BY 4.0 — most distributions carry 'Opendata BY ASK' — so the check's CC-BY-4.0 framing is only partially applicable; the server correctly surfaces the real per-distribution licence rather than hardcoding a licence code, which satisfies the attribution intent.
The global `source`/ATTRIBUTION string names provider+URL but defers the licence code to the per-distribution `licence` field rather than stating one globally (appropriate here since licences vary).
